extracted.intended_audience: current and aspiring Department Chairs (mathematics) and academic administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and standards for running a mathematics department: hiring, faculty rewards, committees, graduate and undergraduate programs, and daily management tasks. Focused on what a Chair should do, delegate, and monitor to keep the department healthy and competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair oversees the entire hiring process: bringing candidates in, arranging talks and interviews, determining their needs, and making the institutional case for offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair should be acquainted with each candidate, ask pointed questions about salary/startup/spousal needs, and manage the sequence (meeting department, giving a talk, meeting the Dean). The Chair typically conducts or chairs the interview with the candidate or the hiring committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess candidate fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate what a candidate can contribute to the research program, the teaching effort, and overall departmental development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider research quality, teaching ability, potential to raise department profile or attract other strong people, and longer-term departmental impact when judging who is 'best' for the Department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make a compelling case to administration
rubrics_metrics.description: After assessing a candidate, the Chair must determine whether the University/Dean can meet the candidate's demands and then persuade the administration to approve the offer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue that the hire is transformative for the department; citing external market interest (e.g., Princeton/Harvard would also make an offer) strengthens the case. Learn the vocabulary of selling candidates to the Dean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary and perks negotiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare to fight over salary level and other perks; Deans may prefer minimal advertised commitments and conservative salaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ready to justify higher salaries for more advanced or tenured candidates; make the competitive-market argument. Consider combinations of salary, startup funds, and other perks to make offers attractive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and accommodate candidate needs (startup, spouse, leaves)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and plan for candidate-specific requests: startup funds, travel/visiting leaves, spouse/significant-other career needs (two-body problem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Startup funds for mathematicians are typically smaller than for lab scientists; Deans may be less sympathetic. Anticipate and negotiate these items; recognize that two-body problems may require creative solutions or additional positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visiting candidate evaluation practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide what hoops visiting candidates should jump through (seminar, teaching demonstration, meetings with committees/students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard practice: candidate gives a talk and is taken to dinner; teaching demos (e.g., calculus lecture) can be tried but may irritate candidates and be low yield. Meetings with teaching committees or informal social activities can provide additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure fair hearing and manage departmental emotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guarantee that all candidates get a fair hearing and that lively departmental opinions are managed constructively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair must supervise big egos, hurt feelings, and partisan advocacy; ensure everyone is heard, present merits of all sides, and prevent attacks from derailing objective evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use long-range planning to smooth hiring
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a Long-Range Planning Committee to take a long view on hiring and to smooth departmental hiring strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A planning body can reduce impulsive or excessively partisan hiring choices and help align hires with longer-term departmental priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative Action compliance and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare and maintain an Affirmative Action dossier for each advertised job showing search statistics and steps taken to ensure fairness and inclusiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can require extra staff work (spreadsheets, targeted ads, tracking). Mishandling may lead the Dean to pull the plug on a hire very late in the process; take this seriously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider reduced teaching load as a recruitment tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer reduced teaching loads (often for the first year or two) as one perk to attract candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deans may or may not support this formally; chairs sometimes accomplish it 'under the table' by rearranging departmental teaching assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle two-body problems proactively
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that candidates often have partners with career needs and that solving two-body problems may be critical to securing hires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deans may pay lip service to solving two-body issues but be reluctant to produce additional positions; be prepared to advocate creatively and recognize limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an Executive Committee (about five senior faculty) to advise, provide perspective, act as a buffer, and assist with manageable tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Committee to bounce ideas, navigate complex situations, and deflect responsibility when appropriate. Typically elected by the Department, refreshed each year, and used with restraint for legwork or information-gathering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegate to dedicated staff (secretaries, IT, library)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on secretaries for undergraduate and graduate affairs, computer support staff, and the Departmental Librarian to manage operational detail and keep a finger on the pulse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult these agents regularly; they often know more about day-to-day functioning than Vice-Chairs. Proactively address computing needs and library issues; plan ahead to secure equipment or systems when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a fair reward system
rubrics_metrics.description: Work to ensure departmental reward structures (raises, promotions, recognition) fairly value research, teaching, service, and other contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge research's high profile in mathematics but also recognize teaching, curricular work, and service. Collaborate with the Dean to allocate resources; consider frameworks like Carnegie Foundation recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Celebrate faculty and staff achievements
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicly acknowledge prizes and awards for faculty and staff to make people feel important and appreciated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congratulate recipients personally, ask about the prize, organize departmental celebrations (tea, speeches), and make special efforts for staff awards to show appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster relations with other departments and interdisciplinarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid departmental isolation; engage in interdisciplinary programs and campus-wide collaborations to improve standing with the Dean and access funding/resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate in consortia of Chairs, jointly lobby the Dean for shared resources (e.g., computing, research offices), and demonstrate the department as a team player to avoid negative administrative perceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appoint and support Vice-Chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Designate Vice-Chairs (Undergraduate, Graduate, Administrative) to oversee distinct missions, relieve administrative burden, and advise the Chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select trusted colleagues, offer perks (salary boost, teaching relief, equipment), consult them on hiring/promotion matters, and treat the relationship symbiotically to derive maximum benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use committees and ensure inclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Form committees for decisions affecting the whole department; spread responsibility and ensure junior faculty representation to avoid disenfranchisement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist the temptation to do everything personally; regular faculty meetings and committee deliberations create buy-in and distribute authority. Avoid stacking committees only with allies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and advocate for graduate students
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure graduate stipends are competitive, recruit top students, treat students well, and listen to their concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with the Vice-Chair for Graduate Studies on recruitment activities (visits, presentations), consider signing bonuses or competitive packages, and engage constructively with student leaders (including unionization issues in some institutions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Define Graduate Vice-Chair responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify that the Graduate Vice-Chair oversees admissions, qualifying exams, thesis advisor matching, student progress, and stipend administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect the Graduate Vice-Chair to organize admitted-student recruitment events, work with a Graduate Committee and secretary, and develop strategies to attract top students (advertising, faculty advocacy while traveling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Actively recruit and grow undergraduate majors
rubrics_metrics.description: Design programs and initiatives to attract and retain undergraduate majors, thereby gaining the Dean's attention and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: create interdisciplinary or computational majors, 'roll your own' majors, improve advising, have faculty promote the major in large classes, host events, and send targeted communications to prospective majors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define Undergraduate Vice-Chair responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Charge the Undergraduate Vice-Chair with overseeing majors, curriculum, graduation tasks, awards, course web pages/syllabi, and handling student complaints and advising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the Vice-Chair with an advisory committee and sufficient delegation; recognize the visibility of this role and choose a person who represents the department well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor the aggregate of mathematics and allied courses to ensure the curriculum meets students' needs and is competitive and contemporary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how the curriculum compares to peer departments and allied fields (Physics, CS, Engineering), ensure prerequisites and course requirements are appropriate, and use the Undergraduate Vice-Chair and curriculum committees to keep the program current.
